title: Jira from code
bridge: Jira's REST API v3 is like the GitHub API you used with Octokit: JSON over HTTPS with a token. Except: we use no typed client, only fetch through shared/src/jira.ts. Search takes JQL and pages with a nextPageToken, and comments are ADF trees, not markdown.
intro: Nova finds its tickets, its requester and its commands in Jira, all by polling. This lesson writes the few calls that needs. Search with JQL, read and write issue properties, read the changelog, and respect Jira's rate limits. It is the code behind G3-28's poll and G4-04's hand-off.

picture.caption: Search finds the ticket, and a property or the changelog names the requester. The run starts with that person as owner.

steps.text: JQL: assignee = currentUser(), as the Nova service account; page with nextPageToken
was it handed over in Slack? then nova.requester holds the person
otherwise: the author of the latest change that set assignee to Nova
startRun with the Handoff; no requester found means no run

p: Every Jira user has an accountId, a long ID like 712020:4c1d0e.... The API uses it everywhere: assignee, comment author, changelog author. GET /rest/api/3/myself tells you yours. For Nova this is the Nova service account, a Jira user that belongs to a program.

On your own free site you call Jira with Basic auth: your email and an API token. Nova uses a scoped token of its service account, stored in Vault infrastructure/ai-agents/jira-nova and synced only to the orchestrator workers. Scoped tokens go through api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<cloudId>; G4-04 says to check this. A VM never holds a Jira token: inside a run, the broker's one-issue scope is used.
sections.ifInstead: If instead you get 401, the email and token do not match, or the token was copied with a space. Create a new token and export it again.

sections.h: One fetch function for every call
p: We use Node's global fetch, wrapped once in shared/src/jira.ts. The wrapper adds the auth header, turns errors into exceptions, and handles two cases every caller needs. A 404 becomes undefined, because a missing property is normal. A 429 means too many requests: Jira's Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait.
Temporal adds a second layer. startMatches runs with the PEOPLE_APIS retry policy, so a Jira outage is also retried at the activity level (p7-2).
sections.because: We wrap fetch once because auth, rate limits and errors must behave the same in every Jira call.

notes.text: The site URL. With a scoped service-account token it is the api.atlassian.com form; check G4-04.
Basic auth is email:token in base64. The token comes from the environment, never from code.
429: Jira is rate limiting us. Retrying at once would make it worse.
Retry-After is in seconds. Wait exactly that, then try again.
404 is an answer, not an error, for lookups like issue properties.
Anything else that is not 2xx throws. The activity's retry policy takes it from there.
204 No Content has no body, for example after setting the assignee.

p: JQL, Jira Query Language, is the filter text you type in Jira's search box. Nova's is project = RH AND assignee = currentUser() AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY updated ASC. currentUser() is whoever calls the API, so for the service account it means Nova.

The search endpoint is POST /rest/api/3/search/jql. The older /rest/api/3/search with startAt is retired. Each page returns issues and, if there is more, a nextPageToken; send it back to get the next page. Ask only for the fields you need: it is faster, and it keeps data we must not see out of the response.
sections.because: We page until nextPageToken is gone because a poll that reads only the first page silently drops tickets.

notes.text: The page shape we use: the issues, and a token when another page exists.
fields: only what the poll needs. Never attachments: they may hold customer data.
POST with a JSON body, not GET with a query string, so long JQL fits.
maxResults is a request; Jira may return fewer. nextPageToken is undefined on the first call.
No token means the last page.

sections.h: Issue properties: hidden notes on a ticket
p: An issue property is a small JSON value an app stores on an issue under a key. People do not see it in the UI, and it does not notify anyone. Nova uses one: nova.requester, set when someone hands a ticket over with /nova in Slack.
Then the Slack hand-off looks exactly like a Jira hand-off: the property names the person, and the ticket is assigned to Nova. The poll does the rest, the same way for both.
sections.because: We store the Slack requester as a property because our app makes that assignee change. So the changelog would not name the person.

notes.text: The property key goes in the URL, so encode it.
The GET returns { key, value }. Missing: 404, so undefined.
PUT stores any JSON value. A string is fine.
dana.jira: her accountId from config/people.yaml (p9-1).
Assigning to Nova is what the poll looks for. The property tells it who asked.

p: Jira keeps a changelog per issue: every field change with its author and time, oldest first. Each entry has items, one per field: field, from and to. For the assignee field, from and to are accountIds.

requesterOf reads it when there is no property. It keeps the entries that set the assignee to Nova and takes the last one's author. If someone unassigned and assigned again, the latest person is the requester. No entry means no requester, and no run starts.
sections.because: We read the changelog because Jira records who assigned the ticket, and that person must own the run.

notes.text: One changed field. For assignee, to is the new assignee's accountId.
This endpoint pages with startAt and isLast, unlike search.
The Slack path first: the property set by /nova.
jira.me is Nova's own accountId, read once from /myself.
The last matching entry: the most recent hand-over wins.

p: Writing back is three calls. POST /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment adds a comment, PUT .../comment/{id} edits it, and PUT .../assignee changes the assignee. Comment bodies are ADF, Atlassian Document Format: a JSON tree of paragraphs, text and mention nodes.

Nova keeps one status comment per ticket and edits it with notifyUsers=false, so watchers are not pinged at every step (G4-11). It assigns the ticket back to the requester when the PR is marked ready, so a person always owns it (G4-05).

callout.text: PHI never enters a prompt. The broker's Jira scope returns summary, description and comments only, never attachments such as screenshots or logs.

p: One direction only: we call Jira, Jira never calls us. Poll on a schedule with overlap SKIP, so a slow poll never stacks (p7-5). Make every action idempotent: startRun's workflow ID turns the 60th sighting of a ticket into nothing.

Order by updated ASC, so the oldest change is handled first. Ask for few fields, page to the end, and honour Retry-After. Never react to Nova's own comments or assignee changes, or Nova talks to itself. parseCommand skips Nova's author ID, and Nova's assign-back is not a stop.

callout.text: To read @Nova commands, the poll lists open ticketToPr runs with a visibility query and reads only those tickets' new comments (G4-05).

lab.title: Find your requester in a real Jira
youNeed: A free Jira Cloud site of your own (atlassian.com, Jira Free), never the company site
An API token from id.atlassian.com, Security, API tokens

worked.do: In your site, open the project the site created and note its key (for example KAN). Create two issues by hand: KAN-1 and KAN-2.
worked.see: Two issues in the board's first column

worked.do: Create src/jira.ts with jiraFetch, searchAll, issueProperty, setIssueProperty and changelog from the blocks above. Define JiraIssue as { key: string; fields: Record<string, unknown> }.
Create src/jira-lab.ts that prints (await searchAll('project = KAN ORDER BY updated ASC')).map((i) => i.key). Run: npx tsx src/jira-lab.ts
In Jira, assign KAN-1 to yourself, then to Unassigned, then to yourself again
worked.see: Three entries in the issue's History tab

worked.do: Print the changelog: for each change, author.accountId and the assignee items' from and to
Write requesterOf with jira.me set to your own accountId and run it for KAN-1, then for KAN-2

lab.faded: Hand KAN-2 over the Slack way: setIssueProperty('KAN-2', 'nova.requester', '<an accountId>') from a script. Left to you: run requesterOf('KAN-2') again and explain which branch of the function answered.
lab.alone: Write pollOnce(jql) that searches, and for each issue logs 'start lab:<key> for <requester>' or 'skip <key>: no requester'. Run it three times in a row and confirm it is safe to repeat. Then lower maxResults to 1 and confirm you still get every issue through nextPageToken.
lab.done: Your code paged through a JQL search, read and wrote an issue property, and named who last assigned a ticket.

quiz.q: A search returns 100 issues and a nextPageToken. What do you do next?

options.text: Send the same request with startAt: 100
options.why: startAt belongs to the retired search endpoint; search/jql pages with tokens.

options.text: Send the same request again with that nextPageToken, until none comes back
options.why: The token is the cursor; no token means the last page.

options.text: Stop: 100 is the most a poll should read
options.why: Then tickets past the first page would never start a run.

quiz.q: Jira answers 429 with Retry-After: 30. What should jiraFetch do?

options.text: Wait 30 seconds, then send the request again
options.why: Honour the header; retrying sooner only extends the limit.

options.text: Retry at once, up to five times
options.why: Hammering a rate-limited API makes the limit last longer.
A rate limit is temporary; the run must not die for it.

quiz.q: Dana assigned RH-7 to Nova, then unassigned it. A day later Omer assigned it to Nova again. Who does requesterOf return?

options.text: Dana, the first person who handed it over
options.why: requesterOf takes the last matching change, not the first.
The reporter is not read at all; only assignee changes to Nova count.

options.text: Omer, the author of the latest change that set the assignee to Nova
options.why: toNova.at(-1): the most recent hand-over wins.

words.plain: Jira Query Language: the filter text that finds issues, like SQL for tickets.
Jira's ID for a user; used for assignees, authors and the changelog.
The cursor search/jql returns when more results exist; send it back for the next page.
A small hidden JSON value an app stores on an issue under a key, like nova.requester.
Jira's per-issue list of every field change, with author and time, oldest first.
The header on a 429 answer that says how many seconds to wait before retrying.
Atlassian Document Format: the JSON tree Jira uses for comment bodies.

tickets.why: Nova's poll runs NOVA_JQL as the service account and finds the requester in a property or the changelog.
orchestrator/src/jira.ts searches with pagination, reads changelogs and comments, and respects rate limits.
/nova sets nova.requester and assigns the ticket; the poll reads new comments for @Nova commands.
One status comment edited with notifyUsers=false, and a Nova state field set through the same client.

remember: Call Jira, never be called: page JQL to the end, honour Retry-After, and find the requester in nova.requester or the changelog.
